text:
olivia parker: hi team, first day! unpacked my M2 MBP and followed the ABM + Kandji steps. Device shows 'Enrolled' in Kandji but I'm seeing a few blockers: macOS shows 'Profile installation failed: certificate chain mismatch', FileVault enable errors with 'Escrow failed: malformed response', and Okta keeps me at 'Device not compliant - missing security profile'. set up on airport lounge wifi (had to accept terms). any pointers?
it-ops: welcome olivia :wave: airport/captive portals are a common culprit. quick checks please (no full serials here):
```
profiles status -type enrollment
sudo fdesetup status
```
Also search Keychain Access for 'Redwood Corporate CA'.

olivia parker: ran them, here's the output:
profiles status -type enrollment: Enrolled to kandji: true; com.redwood.mdm present; com.redwood.security: not found
sudo fdesetup status: FileVault is Off
Keychain: no Redwood CA present

hannah yeo: thanks. certificate chain mismatch and missing CA means the SCEP/PKI step didn't complete — captive portal likely intercepted it. two immediate options: 1) switch to an unproxied network (phone hotspot or RWD-Corp) and visit https://kandji.redwood/setup-cert to force CA install, or 2) we push the missing profile from Kandji and open a temporary admin window so you can approve system extensions and complete escrow. which do you prefer?

olivia parker: i'm at the airport for a few hours and can't reliably tether. please push the profile and temp admin, thanks. last 4 of serial: A7D3
kandji-bot: action queued: push_profile(com.redwood.security) -> awaiting device acknowledgment
it-ops: granted 2-hour temporary admin and pushed remediation. please approve the Kandji prompt when it appears and then check Keychain; after that go to System Settings -> Privacy & Security and click 'Allow' on any system extension prompts. we'll monitor the device in console. ticket NH-20260522-05 created.

olivia parker: got the Kandji popup, accepted profile. saw 'Redwood Corporate CA' in Keychain. two system extension banners popped up; I clicked Allow. re-ran profiles status -> com.redwood.security present. tried `sudo fdesetup enable` and got 'Escrow in progress' then a pop-up asking for my password. entered it and terminal returned 'Escrow completed'. Okta shows compliant after a sync. thanks for the assist! :smile:
it-ops: great — closing NH-20260522-05. notes: captive portal + activation flows can lead to incomplete CA installs; remediation push + temp admin is our standard remote recovery. filing a quick runbook update to mention airport/captive portal steps. :white_check_mark:
